facing, fragment and explosion defaults: weapon_facings defaults to VALID_WEAPON_FACINGS 15 and is masked with 15, and each facing type is read only when its bit is set, default EQ_WEAPON_NONE (ShipEntity.m:298-306; bits forward 1, aft 2, port 4, starboard 8, OOTypes.h:196-206); weapon_position_aft, _port and _starboard default to 0 0 0 (ShipEntity.m:479-481); fragment_chance defaults to 0.9 as a float parameter, so the float32 0.8999999761581421 (ShipEntity.m:372, OOCollectionExtractors.h:152); explosion_type defaults to nil, recorded as null, never [] (ShipEntity.m:491); none of the nine templates authors fragment_chance or explosion_type (the keys appear only on other templates in shipdata.plist)

float32 note: the float32 values (the three new positions and fragmentChance) are computed with Math.fround, the same rounding the converter applies, so this golden is an independent oracle for the authored strings, the line numbers and the mask semantics but not for the rounding

boundingBox (D16-23): the float32 minimum and maximum per axis of each hull's VERTEX block in third_party/oolite/Models/oolite_<key>.dat (Oolite's model axes, no subentity: none of the nine has a solid one), read by an independent scratch Node script that parses the NVERTS count and the VERTEX lines directly and rounds each component with Math.fround, not by the converter; Oolite's drawable box is the same vertex extremes (OOMesh.m:1786-1805, OOEntityWithDrawable.m:55), the box releaseCargoPodsDebris samples (OOVector.m:107-113). Adder: min [-14.0093, -5.19068, -22.2328], max [14.0093, 9.70464, 28.9523] over 1102 vertices; Krait: min [-47.2038, -11.1088, -41.3069], max [47.2038, 10.6843, 41.5081] over 1023 vertices; the other seven come from the same run
